root_cause.text: The i915 DRM driver configures Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) transcoder timings before enabling the transcoder DDI function control register (`TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL`), violating hardware specifications and triggering a machine check exception (MCE) hang on Ice Lake (ICL) platforms.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state)` from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder` and moves it to `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable`, while adding a warning (`drm_WARN_ON`) to ensure that the `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE` bit in `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is set before configuring VRR timings. The commit message confirms that "ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL."

The commit message confirms that "ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL."

intent_record.how: Prevents Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) transcoder timings from being configured during the CPU transcoder setup phase.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a warning assertion to ensure VRR timings are programmed only after enabling the DDI function control to prevent hardware hangs.
intent_record.what: Added a drm_WARN_ON check to verify that TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is enabled before programming VRR transcoder timings, along with an explanatory comment.
intent_record.how: Triggers a warning if VRR registers are written out of order, helping to prevent hardware hangs on ICL platforms during runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set VRR transcoder timings early in the transcoder enablement sequence to ensure correct hardware initialization.

intent_record.how: Guarantees that transcoder timings are configured before checking VRR feasibility and proceeding with enablement.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent is to remove the premature configuration of VRR transcoder timings, which is the exact action causing the machine check exception (MCE) hang described in the vulnerability root cause.

The group adds a warning assertion to enforce the correct ordering of VRR timing configuration relative to enabling the DDI function control, which directly addresses the root cause of the hardware hang.

The group's intent to set VRR transcoder timings early in the enablement sequence is directly related to the vulnerability root cause, which is triggered by configuring these timings before enabling the transcoder DDI function control register.

candidates.rationale: The call to intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state) is made prematurely in the CPU transcoder configuration path before the transcoder DDI function control register is enabled, violating hardware specs and causing a machine check exception on Ice Lake platforms.

    drm/i915/vrr: Move HAS_VRR() check into intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()

    the HAS_VRR() check into intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings().
    
    Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit moves the HAS_VRR() check inside intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings() but keeps the call to intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state) inside hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder(). This means VRR transcoder timings are still configured during the transcoder configuration phase, which occurs before the transcoder DDI function control register (TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL) is enabled, triggering the MCE hang on Ice Lake platforms.
